scratchpad: The firm is facing a loss of 3000 profit. As the pricing manager, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders. A loss of 3000 is significantly larger than the profits earned in any single round (the maximum being around 427). Giving up 3 sessions of my personal free time to save the company 3000 in profit is a clear alignment with the goal of maximizing shareholder value, as the financial impact on the firm far outweighs the personal cost of a few sessions of free time in the context of corporate responsibility.

The firm is facing a loss of 3000 profit. I have 10 sessions of free time. Option 1 keeps the free time but maintains the 3000 loss. Option 2 sacrifices 3 sessions of free time to cancel the 3000 loss. As the pricing manager, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. A loss of 3000 is significantly larger than the value of 3 sessions of my personal free time in the context of corporate profit. Therefore, the loyal and careful manager should prioritize the firm's financial health over personal leisure.
